title: What Class 4 Shingles Really Mean
description: Class 4 is a lab test with a 2-inch steel ball, not a promise that hail will leave your roof alone.
html:
“Class 4” gets printed on the estimate like it ends the hail conversation. It does not. It tells you how that shingle sample behaved in a specific test. That is useful. It is not a force field.

The test, in plain language

UL 2218 drops a steel ball on a roofing sample, twice, in the same spot. Class 4 is the top of that scale: a 2-inch ball from 20 feet, without a crack that opens the back of the sample. Class 3 uses a smaller ball from a lower drop. The test is done in a lab, on a new sample, at a set temperature. Your roof sees odd angles, older asphalt, and hail that is not a perfect sphere.

A Class 4 shingle resists fracture better than a basic architectural shingle. Large hail can still bruise it. Small hail can still knock granules off. The rating is about impact cracks, not about looks, and not about wind.

The insurance discount is not automatic

Some carriers credit a Class 4 roof. Some do not. Some credit it only if the whole roof is Class 4, documented, and installed to the maker’s spec. We do not quote you a discount. Your agent does, from your policy. Ask them before you buy the shingle for the discount alone.

Installation still decides the roof

A Class 4 shingle on a short valley, a reused flashing, or a nail driven through the sealant strip will leak for reasons the steel-ball test never measured. The rating is about the shingle. The roof is the shingle plus the underlayment, the starter, the hips, and the metal. We install Class 4 to the maker’s pattern when that is the shingle you choose, because a discounted or denied material warranty is a bad trade for a line on a brochure.

What we will tell you is whether Class 4 asphalt shingles makes sense on your house: the slopes, the hail you have already taken, and whether metal roofs or stone-coated steel is the better answer for the same money. Request a free inspection if you want that comparison on your actual roof. (281) 541-0027.
